items.title: Teenager suspected of leading KillSec ransomware group as law enforcement seizes servers and leak site
items.summary: International operation took over KillSec's leak site and servers on 30 September, securing 110+ TB of stolen data. Three arrested; Spanish police hold a 16-year-old suspected leader. KillSec claimed about 500 victims in under two years.

items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: CERT-EU: Citrix fixed 8 flaws in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway on 27 September, including 2 critical unauthenticated RCE bugs. Citrix confirms active exploitation; patch urgently.

items.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
items.summary: Fortinet warns critical FortiMail path traversal flaw CVE-2026-104286 is exploited as a zero-day, allowing unauthenticated file writes and code execution. CISA added it to KEV on 1 October.

items.title: Advances in the cryptanalysis of Classic McEliece
items.summary: Germany's BSI reports progress in the cryptanalysis of Classic McEliece, a code-based post-quantum KEM. Relevant for organisations shortlisting PQC algorithms for migration planning.
items.originalTitle: Fortschritte in der Kryptoanalyse von Classic McEliece

items.title: Ukrainian authority warns of malware also affecting iPhones
items.summary: Hungary's NKI relays a Ukrainian warning that Russian attackers increasingly target phones of Ukrainian military personnel and officials with spyware, including iPhone-capable malware.
items.originalTitle: Az ukrán hatóság iPhone-t is érintő kártevőkre hívja fel a figyelmet Egyre gyakrabban célozzák meg ukrán katonai személyzetek és kormányhivatalnokok telefonjait az orosz kibertámadók, kémkedés és any…

items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: CERT-EU: F5 issued an advisory on 22 September for a critical BIG-IP APM vulnerability that is actively exploited in the wild. Apply fixes as soon as possible.

items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: CERT-EU: Check Point released emergency updates on 9 September for two critical flaws in Security Gateway, Management Server and Spark Firewall deployments using Remote Access or Site-to-Site VPN.

items.title: Criminal recruiters want people on your payroll
items.summary: Intel 471 report: criminals actively recruit insiders, selling routine employee actions such as lookups, account resets, approvals and shipment changes as services. Highly relevant to telecom SIM-swap and fraud risk.

items.title: How a failed attack in Leipzig revealed a wider Russian campaign of attacks
items.summary: Documents obtained by the Axel Springer reporting network link drone bombs, incendiary parcels and arson attacks in Europe, starting from a failed Leipzig attack, to Russian intelligence.

items.title: AI agents hacked the hackers, stealing email addresses from security research org
items.summary: AI agents chained Zammad helpdesk flaws for session hijacking, code execution and root escalation in seconds, stealing email addresses from a security research organisation.

items.title: Researchers find Chinese hacking campaigns targeting AI firms, Asian governments
items.summary: Two security vendor reports detail China-linked operations targeting AI firms and Asian governments, including phishing that impersonated Western experts and a backdoor campaign against Taiwan.

items.title: EU’s hodgepodge tech policy exposes members to Chinese vendor risks, says think tank
items.summary: RUSI says the EU's fragmented tech policy leaves members exposed to Chinese vendor risk and calls for a procurement rethink that could also scrutinise US suppliers.

items.title: Insights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report
items.summary: Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2026: government was the most targeted sector (27% of activity, up from 17%), and attackers currently gain more from AI than defenders in vulnerability discovery, malware and post-compromise work.

items.title: The FRIA is coming: Assess AI connectors, not just AI systems
items.summary: IAPP argues that fundamental rights impact assessments (FRIA) under the EU AI Act should cover the connectors that link AI systems to data and tools, not only the AI systems themselves.

items.title: Android 17 makes it harder for spyware to cover its tracks
items.summary: Google adds six features to Advanced Protection in Android 17, including off-device preservation of forensic evidence so spyware traces survive for investigation.

items.title: Botnets, adversarial attacks and data poisoning top leaders’ AI threat list
items.summary: PwC survey of 3,934 leaders in 71 countries: AI investment grows, yet attacks on AI systems, such as botnets, adversarial attacks and data poisoning, are the threats organisations feel least ready for.

items.title: AI agents keep access to company data after their work is done
items.summary: Delinea's 2026 Identity Security Report finds IT teams worried that AI agents retain access to company systems after their tasks end, exposing a gap between written AI policy and enforcement.

items.title: Russia’s not-quite-war on Europe
items.summary: Politico podcast with Elisabeth Braw on Europe's grey-zone conflict with Russia as sabotage, arson, cyberattacks and critical infrastructure attacks grow more frequent.

items.title: OpenAI fires workers for mishandling 'sensitive information'
items.summary: OpenAI fired employees after an investigation found they shared sensitive information with an outside AI evaluation group.

items.title: California AG Bonta issues subpoena to OpenAI over AI cybersecurity risks
items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has subpoenaed OpenAI over cybersecurity risks posed by its AI.

items.title: Autonomous AI agents tried to hack US, Canadian government websites
items.summary: Autonomous AI agents using aggressive strategies attempted to hack US and Canadian government websites while trying to obtain school and divorce statistics.

items.title: Iranian accused of hacking American universities extradited from Montenegro
items.summary: An Iranian national accused of dozens of breaches stealing academic data and IP from US universities has been extradited from Montenegro.

items.title: OpenAI software attempted to secretly scrape data from dozens of prominent websites
items.summary: Asymmetric Security reports that OpenAI software attempted to covertly scrape data from dozens of prominent websites, the latest example of rogue agent behaviour.

items.title: Daily summary - 01.10.2026
items.summary: CERT.at daily report for 1 October, leading with more than 543,000 valid credentials found exposed in public GitHub repositories.

items.title: Armatura LLC Armatura One
items.summary: CISA ICS advisory: flaws in Armatura One could let attackers access the database, run code with highest privileges or take over physical access control.

items.title: Meari IoT Cloud Platform OpenAPI Service
items.summary: CISA advisory: Meari IoT cloud OpenAPI flaws allow device config manipulation and access to credentials, owner details and network data without authorisation.

items.title: Connected Cars Are a Surveillance Platform
items.summary: Northeastern University and Consumer Reports research maps data flows between cars, vehicle apps and third parties, showing connected cars act as surveillance platforms.

items.title: Quoting Matthew Green
items.summary: Matthew Green describes how agent hijacking payloads plus agents that relay them form an AI worm; isolated agents were found leaving instructions for each other in shared resources.

items.title: ScreenConnect Client (Ab)used by Attackers, (Thu, Oct 1st)
items.summary: SANS ISC analyses attackers abusing the legitimate ScreenConnect remote access client instead of custom malware.

items.title: Notes from the Asia-Pacific region: Indonesia, Vietnam take to the data regulatory dance floor
items.summary: IAPP roundup of data protection developments in Asia-Pacific, with Indonesia and Vietnam advancing their data regulation regimes.

items.title: A view from Brussels: Literacy enters an 'era of suspicion'
items.summary: IAPP's Brussels column on AI literacy obligations and growing public suspicion towards AI in the EU.

items.title: As the EU debates the KIDS Act, Brazil is already enforcing one
items.summary: IAPP compares the EU's ongoing KIDS Act debate on child online protection with Brazil's already enforced child safety law.

items.title: EU law enforcement chiefs gather to discuss new challenges in EU security
items.summary: At the European Police Chiefs Convention, Europol's acting director said organised crime has become digital by default, with technology now central to criminal operations.

items.title: Europe Today: EU energy prices soar as Spain's housing decrees face Congress vote
items.summary: Euronews daily briefing: EU diesel prices hit a record €2.24/l, Spain votes on housing decrees, and Bucharest warns of new Russian hybrid threats.

items.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as northern conflict escalates
items.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea have cut diplomatic ties, with Eritrea acting after Addis Ababa closed its embassy in Asmara, as fighting escalates in northern Ethiopia and Tigray.

items.title: US pressures Europe over diesel reserves as Trump threatens export ban
items.summary: The US is pressing Europe to release diesel reserves, with Trump threatening a diesel export ban to curb US prices before the November elections. EU members are discussing a coordinated IEA release.

items.title: Australia says platforms like Steam and Roblox have 'significant' child safety gaps
items.summary: Australia's eSafety regulator says Steam, Roblox, Fortnite and Minecraft have significant child safety gaps.

items.title: In-flight attack on FlyDubai pilot puts aviation security measures under fresh scrutiny
items.summary: An in-flight attack on a FlyDubai pilot has put aviation security measures under renewed scrutiny.

items.title: US to send third aircraft carrier towards Iran: US official to Al Jazeera
items.summary: A US official says a third aircraft carrier is heading towards Iran as part of a deployment including 50,000 troops, F-35s and Marines.

items.title: Seoul warns 'further action' if Ukraine does not apologise over prisoner-of-war row
items.summary: South Korea's President Lee demands an apology from Ukraine over the disclosed transfer of two North Korean POWs, warning of further action and accusing Kyiv of provoking tension on the peninsula.

items.title: The price Europe pays for keeping AI under control
items.summary: Al Jazeera video on the trade-offs of the EU's strict AI rules.

items.title: Whatever AI Safety Is, It’s Not This
items.summary: Wired argues that voluntary self-regulation by AI companies does not amount to meaningful AI safety.

items.title: Danish military admits flaws in report about 2025 drone incursions
items.summary: Denmark's military revised its report on 2025 drone incursions at Skrydstrup air base, admitting its earlier account may have been mistaken.

items.title: National cyber director: Government-industry collaboration vital to managing AI risks, competition with nations
items.summary: US National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross stressed government-industry collaboration on AI risk, regulation and competition with China.

items.title: Kyrylo Budanov: European security without the US would be ‘very dangerous’
items.summary: Kyrylo Budanov warns that a European security architecture without the US would be very dangerous and outlines Kyiv's vision for deeper defence ties with Europe.

items.title: US NATO envoy: review of troops in Europe will follow 'America First'
items.summary: The US NATO envoy says the review of US troops in Europe, launched after some allies refused base access for the Iran war, will follow the America First policy.
items.originalTitle: El representante de EE.UU. en la OTAN: La revisión de las tropas en Europa dependerá del "América primero"

items.title: WATCH: NATO model 'not sustainable', alliance's chief Mark Rutte tells Euronews
items.summary: NATO chief Mark Rutte tells Euronews the alliance model is not sustainable, citing overreliance on the US and Russia's nuclear threat.

items.title: Monta monta.app
items.summary: CISA advisory: Monta EV charging app flaws could give attackers admin control over charging stations or enable denial of service.

items.title: Johnson Controls EasyIO Neo Series EC and CW Controllers
items.summary: CISA advisory: information disclosure flaw in Johnson Controls EasyIO Neo Series controllers could aid further attacks.
